one_sentence_failure_summary: The compress.py script places all ~330 batch directories directly under the output root, violating the 30-items-per-directory constraint, because the generated code applies one level of batching but never groups those batch dirs into a second-level hierarchy covering the root itself.
t_err_evidence: At step 8 the agent writes compress.py whose create_hierarchical_structure method splits items into batch_0000, batch_0001, ... subdirectories all placed directly inside dest_dir (the output root). With 9,898 input files and a batch size of 30, this produces ceil(9898/30)=330 batch dirs at the root, exceeding the 30-items-per-directory limit the agent itself documented in step 7.
t_commit_evidence: The flawed compress.py is the only compression script produced and is used in all subsequent test runs (steps 10, 18, 23, 27). No corrective rewrite of compress.py occurs at any point in the trajectory. Once this script is written and executed, the constraint-violating output structure is inevitable for any input with more than 30 files.
t_surface_evidence: Step 12 output: 'ls -la | grep batch | wc -l' returns 330 and the header shows 'drwxr-xr-x 332 root root' for the test_output directory, providing the first explicit numerical confirmation that 330 batch dirs exist at the root (well above the 30-item limit).
trigger_explanation: The agent correctly planned in step 7 that it needs a 'tree-like directory structure where each directory has at most 30 items', but the generated code only applies one level of grouping (files into batch dirs) without a second level that groups the batch dirs themselves. This is a code-generation failure: the stated plan required true multi-level recursion at every directory node including the root, but the implementation provides only single-level batching of leaf files.
